Hi Jonas — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a small info ask so we can put together a tight proposal: 

1) Target SLOs and traffic profile
- Latency: you mentioned 95th < 80ms and 99th < 150ms for short chat turns (~64–128 tokens). For long-form streaming (up to 2k tokens) you want tail latencies under ~300ms per token when streaming. Please confirm those numbers if I misheard.
- Throughput: initial peak concurrent users ~1,200 UUs with expected ramp to 5k over 6 months. Average request size ~600 tokens and burst concurrency factor ~3.
- Concurrency and batching: you preferred low-latency with small batch sizes (2–8) and some tolerance for background batching on non-interactive workloads.

2) Regional routing & residency
- Primary traffic: US (east), secondary EU for EU customers (data residency required), APAC read-only cache + local inference for latency-sensitive users. You said EU patient data must stay inside EU.

3) Integration constraints
- Streaming + function calls support mandatory.
- KV-cache warm start for sessions beneficial — you asked about prefix caching behavior.

Could you share the following so our SEs can size and propose specific options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private):
- Clarify the 99th percentile target for 512- and 2k-token paths (exact ms targets)
- Typical token distribution (percentage of requests in 0–128, 129–512, 513–2000)
- Any hard blocks on cross-border model routing for EU-sensitive customers

I'll loop Marcus from our solutions team for the sizing notes. I'll prepare an SLO matrix and draft routing policy options after I get the token distribution.

Thanks,

Thanks, Olga — great summary. A few clarifications inline: 

- Latency targets: yes — 95th < 80ms; 99th target we'll set at 180ms for the interactive path (0–512 tokens). For streaming (up to 2k) we want token-by-token emission within 220–350ms worst-case on APAC/EU; US should be lower.

- Token distribution (approx): 0–128: 55% | 129–512: 30% | 513–2000: 15%

- Data residency: EU patient PII must remain in-region for inference and logs. We can accept aggregated telemetry (anonymized) to the US but no full request/response export.

- Concurrency: peak concurrency 5k across regions; per-region split ~60% US, 30% EU, 10% APAC.

Jonas / Olga — quick technical notes based on the numbers Jonas provided: 

- Sizing: to hit 99th ~180ms for 0–512 tokens in US and EU with 60/30 split at 5k peak concurrency, we're looking at a Dedicated pool per region (or hosted with pinned capacity) sized roughly to 40–60 A100-equivalent GPUs in US and 20–30 in EU using dynamic batching optimizations and KV cache. APAC can start as a small dedicated edge or regional burst capacity (6–8 GPUs) to meet token emission targets.

- Streaming: to keep per-token emission within ~220–350ms for long-form, we'll enable low-latency kernel paths + async streaming lanes; recommend per-request concurrency limit of 8 tokens inflight for encoder-decoder style models, and continuous KV-cache shard pinned to the same node across the session where possible.

- Routing and residency: We'll implement smart routing rules so EU customer traffic never leaves EU model clusters. For US users we can route to US primary; we suggest a read-replica cache in APAC for non-PII to accelerate token lookups and reduce cross-region hops.

- Fallbacks: configure automatic fallback to smaller quantized variants in a nearby region if local capacity is exhausted, but only for non-PHI customers. For PHI/EU-sensitive flows, fallback to queued or lower-throughput modes (no cross-border fallback).

I'll attach a brief architecture sketch and the SLO worksheet draft. Happy to run numbers in a sizing call.
